home.h1: Christmas light installation and holiday lighting in Southeast Michigan
home.hero_sub: Homes, businesses, HOA entrances and downtowns. We design the display, install it with bucket-truck crews, service it through the season and take it down after the holidays.
home.intro: Holiday Light Service has been putting up lights across Southeast Michigan since 2003. You tell us what you picture. We plan the layout, measure every run, hang each strand in clean, even lines and come back for it after the holidays. No ladder for you. No tangled strands. No weekend lost on a cold roof.
home.services_intro: Rooflines and trees at home, and full-season displays for HOA entrances, businesses and downtowns. Every photo is our own work.

season.label: Book early
season.text: Early requests get the widest choice of install dates. It is also the easiest time to walk the property and plan a design without rushing.

season.label: Design and estimate
season.text: We look at the property, the power and the access, talk through the look you want and send a free estimate that spells out what is included.

season.label: Installation
season.text: Crews hang the display, check connections as they go and test everything before they leave. If weather moves your date, we let you know.

season.label: In-season service

season.label: Takedown
season.text: After the holidays we take everything down with care, so the house goes back to normal for the rest of winter.

reasons: Over two decades of hanging lights on homes, storefronts and downtown streets. We know how rooflines, gutters, trees and Michigan cold behave.
Bucket trucks for the high work
Tall trees, steep peaks and building fronts are reached from the bucket wherever the property allows, instead of from a leaning ladder. That means cleaner lines and less time on the roof.
Design, installation, in-season service and takedown all come from us. One call covers the whole season.
Every display is planned around the architecture, the trees and the view from the street. You get a layout made for your home, not a kit.

services.name: Christmas light installation
services.title: Christmas Light Installation in Southeast Michigan
services.meta_description: Professional Christmas light installation for Southeast Michigan homes. We design, install, service and take down your display. Get a free estimate.
services.h1: Christmas Light Installation in Southeast Michigan
services.hero_sub: Your home, lit in clean lines, with no ladder for you. We design it, hang it, service it through the season and take it down after the holidays.
services.summary: Full-service holiday lighting for your home: design, installation, in-season service and takedown.
services.intro: Hanging Christmas lights yourself means cold hands, a borrowed ladder and a strand that dies halfway across the gutter. We take the whole job off your list. Our crews plan a display around your roofline, trees and entry, install it in clean, even lines and test everything before we leave. If something goes dark during the season, call us. After the holidays we come back and take it all down. You get the lit house without the lost weekend.
scope: A design built around your home
Bistro lighting for patios and porches
considerations: Warm white or multicolor

Warm white reads classic and suits most brick and siding. Multicolor feels playful and nostalgic. Some homes pair a warm white roofline with color in the trees. We will talk through what fits your house and your street.
Power and outlets
Most displays run from existing exterior outlets. We plan the layout around where your power is and how the circuits are shared, which helps keep you from chasing tripped outlets in December.
Book before the rush
Installs commonly run from October into early December. Booking earlier gives you more date options and a better chance of having the display ready before your first holiday gathering.
faqs: When should I book Christmas light installation?

As early as you can. Fall bookings get the widest choice of install dates, and the calendar fills as Thanksgiving gets closer. If you are reading this later in the season, call anyway and we will tell you which dates are left.
What is included in the service?
Design, installation, in-season service and takedown after the holidays. Your estimate spells out exactly what is included for your home, so you know what to expect before the crew arrives.
Do I need to be home for the installation?
Not always. When we schedule, we confirm access to outlets, gates and the areas being lit, and we will tell you if we need you there.
Will installation damage my roof or gutters?
We plan how lights attach to each surface and install with care for shingles, gutters and siding. If anything about your roof needs special handling, we will talk about it during the estimate.
What if a section of lights goes out?
Call us. In-season service is part of what we do, so a dark section means a phone call instead of a trip up the ladder. We will put a service visit on the schedule.
services.cta_line: Get your home on this season's install schedule.

services.name: Roofline Christmas lights
services.title: Roofline Christmas Lights in Southeast Michigan
services.meta_description: Roofline Christmas lights installed in straight, even lines on gutters, peaks and gables. Serving Southeast Michigan since 2003. Get a free estimate.
services.h1: Roofline Christmas Light Installation in Southeast Michigan
services.hero_sub: Straight, even lines along gutters, peaks and gables. It is the first thing people see from the street, so it gets the most care.
services.summary: Crisp lines on gutters, peaks, gables and dormers, with the high sections reached from the bucket truck.
services.intro: The roofline is the frame of your whole display. When the lines sag or the spacing drifts, everyone on the street notices. We measure each run, plan where the power goes and set the lights at an even spacing along gutters, peaks, gables and dormers. Tall and steep sections are reached from the bucket truck. The result is a crisp outline of your house that looks sharp from the curb and from the end of the block.
scope: Warm white, cool white or multicolor
Bucket-truck access for tall and steep sections
considerations: Plan the whole outline
Some houses look sharpest with every edge lit. Others look better with just the front roofline and the peaks. We will show you which lines carry the design and which ones you can skip.
Steep and tall roofs

Two-story peaks and steep pitches are where do-it-yourself lighting gets dangerous. Crews reach the high sections from a bucket truck wherever access allows, which keeps people off the steepest parts of the roof.
Gutters, shingles and trim

Attachment depends on the surface. We plan how the lights mount to gutters, shingles and fascia so the lines stay straight, and we flag anything about your roof that needs special care during the estimate.
faqs: Can you light only the front of the house?
Yes. Many homeowners light the front roofline and the peaks facing the street. We will help you decide where lights make the biggest difference for the budget you have in mind.
What color options do I have?
Warm white is a classic choice for rooflines. Cool white reads crisp and modern. Multicolor brings a nostalgic feel. You can also mix, such as a warm white roofline with color in the trees.
Can you reach a two-story or steep roof?
Yes. Our crews use bucket trucks for tall peaks and steep sections, so high work is done from the lift wherever the property allows. We check access during the estimate.
Do you take the roofline lights down?
Yes. Takedown after the holidays is part of the service. Your estimate spells out what is included for your home.
Should I consider permanent roofline lighting instead?
If you want lights on your roofline for more than the holidays, permanent lighting may fit better. It mounts in a discreet track and runs from an app all year. Ask about both during your estimate.
services.cta_line: Get a crisp roofline without climbing a ladder.

services.name: Tree and shrub lighting
services.title: Tree and Shrub Lighting in Southeast Michigan
services.meta_description: Tree wraps, canopy lighting and shrub lighting for Southeast Michigan homes and properties. Trunks, limbs and evergreens lit with care. Free estimates.
services.h1: Tree and Shrub Lighting in Southeast Michigan
services.hero_sub: Wrapped trunks, lit canopies and glowing evergreens. The trees are often the part of the display people remember.
services.summary: Trunk and limb wraps, canopy lighting and evergreen lighting that gives the whole yard depth.
services.intro: A roofline tells people where the house is. The trees make it feel like the holidays. We wrap trunks and major limbs in tight, even spirals, light canopies from the bucket truck, and drape evergreens and shrubs so the whole yard has depth at night. A single mature tree can anchor the whole display. Smaller shrubs and hedges tie the display together at ground level. Everything comes down after the season, so nothing is left on the branches.
considerations: Wraps or canopy
Wrapping trunks and main limbs gives a tight, sculptural look that reads well up close. Lighting the canopy spreads a softer glow that carries from down the street. Many properties use both.
Tree size and access
Tall trees need a bucket truck to wrap high limbs evenly. Tell us about fences, soft lawns or tight side yards so we can plan how the truck reaches each tree.
Bare trees and evergreens
Bare maples and oaks show off a wrapped trunk and limbs, while spruce and pine look fullest with strands worked through the boughs. A mix of both gives the yard depth from the curb and up close.
faqs: Can you light very tall trees?
Yes. Our crews use bucket trucks to reach high limbs and canopies, as far as access on your property allows. We look at reach and ground conditions during the estimate.
Does wrapping lights hurt the tree?
Lights are wrapped for one season and removed after the holidays, so nothing stays on to restrict growth. We wrap with the branch structure in mind and skip limbs that are too small or brittle.
Should I light every tree in the yard?
Not always. A few fully lit trees often look better than many half-lit ones. We will suggest which trees carry the design from the street and where to focus your budget.
Can you light evergreens and shrubs too?
Yes. Evergreens, hedges and foundation shrubs are a big part of most displays. They fill in the ground level and connect the trees to the house.
Can the trees match my roofline?
Yes. We plan colors across the whole display, so warm white trees sit well with a warm white roofline, or color in the trees plays off a white outline.
services.cta_line: Show us your trees. We will plan the glow.

services.name: Commercial holiday lighting
services.title: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Southeast Michigan
services.meta_description: Commercial Christmas lights and holiday lighting for Southeast Michigan downtowns, shopping centers, HOAs and businesses, from design to removal.
services.h1: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Southeast Michigan
services.hero_sub: Building outlines, tree wraps, canopy lighting and entrance displays for properties that need to be noticed in December.
services.summary: Full-season lighting for businesses, shopping centers, HOAs and downtowns, from walkthrough to removal.
services.intro: In December, storefronts, shopping centers and downtowns all compete for attention, and a dark building looks closed. We design commercial holiday lighting around how people actually approach your property: by car, on foot and from across the street. Then we install it with bucket-truck crews, service it through the season and remove it afterward. You get one contact, one plan and a display that looks deliberate from the parking lot to the front door.
scope: Bistro string lighting for patios and walkways
considerations: Plan around your hours
Installation and removal are scheduled with your traffic in mind. We talk through business hours, deliveries, events and parking before the crew arrives.
Power and lift access
Commercial displays often cover long runs and several power sources. The walkthrough maps outlets, circuits and bucket-truck access so installation day starts with a plan.
Several sites, one plan
If you manage more than one building, center or block, we can plan them together, with one estimate and one point of contact for the season.
faqs: When should businesses book commercial holiday lighting?

Earlier than homeowners. Commercial displays take more planning, and many properties want lights up before the busiest shopping weeks. Walkthroughs in late summer and early fall give you the most options. Later requests are still worth a call, and we will be straight about what can fit this season.
Do you do a site walkthrough?
Yes. Commercial projects start with a walkthrough to look at the buildings, trees, power and lift access. The concept design and estimate come out of that visit.
Can you work around our business hours?
Yes. We plan installation and removal around your hours, deliveries and events wherever possible, and confirm the schedule with you before the crew arrives.
What does commercial service include?
Design, installation, in-season service and removal. Your estimate spells out the scope for your property, including what gets lit and how in-season service works.
Do you light HOA entrances and municipal properties?
Yes. We light subdivision and HOA entrances, downtown streets and municipal properties, as well as offices and shopping centers. Each has its own page with more detail.
services.cta_line: Book a walkthrough for your property.

services.name: Permanent lighting
services.title: Permanent Christmas Lights in Southeast Michigan
services.meta_description: Permanent Christmas lights for Southeast Michigan homes: a discreet track under the eaves with app-controlled colors and schedules, all year.
services.h1: Permanent Roofline Lighting in Southeast Michigan
services.hero_sub: Permanent holiday lights that live under your eaves all year. Pick the colors and the schedule from your phone, for Christmas, game days or every night.
services.summary: App-controlled lighting in a discreet track under the eaves, installed once and used all year.
services.intro: Permanent lighting mounts in a low-profile track under your eaves, where it stays discreet during the day. At night, you choose the colors, scenes and schedule from a smartphone app. Warm white for the holidays, team colors for game day, soft accent light on an ordinary Tuesday. There is no ladder season and no takedown. We design the layout around your roofline, install the track and lights, and show you how the app works.
scope: A layout planned around your roofline
Discreet track mounted under the eaves
Schedules for holidays, game days and events
considerations: Where the track goes
The track follows your roofline under the eaves. We plan runs, corners and power so the lights read as one clean outline at night and the hardware stays low profile during the day.
Permanent or seasonal
If you only want lights in December, seasonal installation may make more sense. If you would use them for more holidays, events or everyday accent lighting, permanent lighting earns its place.
Check with your HOA
Some associations have rules about exterior lighting and permanent fixtures. Your estimate describes the layout and hardware, which gives your board something concrete to consider.
faqs: Can you see the track during the day?
The track mounts under the eaves and sits low profile, so it is discreet from the street. We will talk through how it will look against your trim during the estimate.
How do I control the lights?
From a smartphone app. You can change colors, choose scenes and schedule the lights to turn on and off for holidays, events or every evening.
Are permanent Christmas lights only for Christmas?
No, and that is the point. Use it for Christmas, Halloween, the Fourth of July, game days, birthdays or simple warm white accent lighting all year.
How is permanent lighting priced?
It depends on the length of your roofline, the number of runs and corners, and where power is available. We measure and send a free estimate that spells out what is included.
Should I choose permanent or seasonal lights?
Choose seasonal if you want a classic December display and nothing the rest of the year. Choose permanent if you would use your lights for more occasions. Our guide compares the two in detail.
services.cta_line: Get a permanent lighting estimate for your roofline.

services.name: Landscape lighting
services.title: Landscape Lighting in Southeast Michigan
services.meta_description: Landscape lighting for Southeast Michigan homes and properties. Accent the architecture, trees and paths after dark, all year long. Get a free estimate.
services.hero_sub: Light the house, the trees and the path to the door, so your property looks as good at 9 p.m. as it does at noon.
services.summary: Year-round lighting that brings out architecture, trees and walkways after dark.
services.intro: Your property does not disappear when the sun goes down, but most of it goes dark. Landscape lighting brings it back. We place and aim fixtures to show off the stone, columns and texture of the house, the shape of your trees and planting beds, and the path from the driveway to the front door. The goal is a warm, balanced look, never a floodlit yard. It works all year and pairs well with holiday lighting in December.
scope: Accent lighting for trees and specimen plantings
A layout designed around how you use the space
considerations: Start with how you use it
Think about where you walk, sit and park after dark, and what you want to see from inside the house. That shapes where the light goes.
Less glare, more depth
Good landscape lighting feels balanced. We aim for soft pools of light and highlighted features, not bright spots that wash everything out or shine into a neighbor's windows.
Plan it with the holidays
If you also want holiday lighting, we can plan both together, so the December display works with your landscape fixtures instead of competing with them.
faqs: What is landscape lighting?

Outdoor lighting that highlights your home and yard after dark: uplighting on walls and trees, accent lighting on plantings, and path lighting for walkways and steps. It stays in place and works all year.
Is landscape lighting only about looks?
No. Lighting walkways, steps and entries helps you and your guests see where you are going, and a lit property looks cared for after dark.
Do you design the layout?
Yes. We look at the property, talk through what you want to highlight and plan fixture placement before anything is installed. Your estimate spells out what is included.
Can I combine landscape and holiday lighting?
Yes. Some homeowners start with holiday lighting and add landscape lighting later, or the other way around. Planning both together keeps the property looking consistent all year.
When is a good time to install landscape lighting?
Spring through fall is the easiest time to work in beds and lawns, before the ground freezes. Call anytime to start planning, and we will talk through timing for your property.
services.cta_line: Plan a property that looks good after dark.

verticals.title: Downtown Holiday Lighting | Holiday Light Service
verticals.meta_description: Holiday lighting for Michigan downtowns, main streets and municipal properties. Tree wraps, lamppost decor and district plans, installed and removed.
verticals.h1: Downtown and Municipal Holiday Lighting in Southeast Michigan
verticals.hero_sub: Wrapped street trees, lit lampposts and a main street that draws people out on a December night.
verticals.intro: A well-lit downtown gives people a reason to come out after dark in the coldest weeks of the year. We work with downtown development authorities, city staff and business associations to plan lighting block by block, from wrapped street trees and lamppost decor to the centerpiece tree for the tree lighting. Bucket-truck crews install around traffic and parking, we service the display through the season, and we take it all down afterward.
needs: A plan the whole district can follow
Downtown lighting has many stakeholders. We lay out the design in terms everyone can follow: which blocks, which trees, which poles and what it takes to power them.
Work around traffic and events
Street work is scheduled around parking, events and business hours, with lift work planned to keep sidewalks and lanes as open as possible.
One contact all season
Installation, in-season service and removal come from one company, so city staff have one call to make when something needs attention.
scope: Street tree trunk and canopy wraps
Building outlines on civic and historic buildings
Bistro string lighting over walkways and patios
faqs: When should a downtown start planning holiday lighting?

Well before fall. Budgets, approvals and board meetings take time, and lighting is usually expected to be up for a tree lighting or holiday event. Starting in summer or early fall gives the most flexibility. A later start is still worth a call, and we will tell you what can be done this season.
Can you work with our DDA or city staff?
Yes. We can walk the district with your team, answer questions from a board or committee and put the plan in writing for approval.
Do you service the lights during the season?
Yes. In-season service is part of the plan. If a section goes dark, one call to us gets it on the schedule.
verticals.summary: Street tree wraps, lamppost decor and centerpiece trees for downtowns and municipal properties, planned block by block.
verticals.cta_line: Walk the district with us and start this season's plan.

verticals.h1: HOA and Subdivision Entrance Lighting in Southeast Michigan
verticals.hero_sub: The first thing residents and guests see, lit with care for the whole holiday season.
verticals.intro: The entrance sets the tone for the whole community. We light entrance signs, trees, shrubs and landscape islands so the neighborhood looks cared for every evening of the season. For boards and property managers, we keep it simple: one walkthrough, a clear plan to share with the board, then installation, in-season service and removal. The same process works for a small condominium association or a large subdivision.
needs: A plan the board can approve
Your estimate describes what gets lit and what is included, so the board weighs one clear plan instead of a rough idea.
Power at the entrance
Many entrances have limited outlets. We check the power available at the sign and landscaping, design around it and flag anything that needs attention before the season.
The same look every year
Once the board likes the design, the same plan can be repeated next season, with adjustments if the landscaping changes.
scope: Trees and evergreens at the entrance
faqs: Can you present the plan to our board?
Yes. We can walk the entrance with a board member or manager and provide a written plan and estimate for the board to consider.
Can you light more than one entrance?
Yes. Many subdivisions have two or more entrances. We can plan them together so they match.
Can residents book lighting for their own homes?
Yes. Residents can request their own Christmas light installation estimate, separate from the entrance plan.
verticals.summary: Entrance signs, trees and landscape islands for HOAs, condominiums and subdivisions, with a plan the board can approve.

verticals.h1: Retail and Shopping Center Holiday Lighting in Southeast Michigan
verticals.hero_sub: Rooflines, trees, poles and entrances lit so shoppers see you from the road and feel it at the door.
verticals.intro: During the holidays, a shopping center is judged from the road. Dark parking lot trees and a plain facade read as closed, while a lit property feels busy and worth the stop. We plan retail holiday lighting around the sightlines from the main road, the parking lot and the storefront entrances, then install around your tenants' hours. Property managers get one plan, one contact and a display that is serviced through the season.
needs: Visibility from the road
Building outlines, tall trees and pole decor carry the farthest. We focus the plan on what drivers see first.
Scheduling that respects tenants
Installation and removal are planned around store hours, deliveries and parking, with lift work kept away from busy entrances where possible.
One plan across the property
Multiple buildings, outparcels and entrances are designed together, so the center looks like one place.
faqs: When should a shopping center book holiday lighting?

Early. Centers usually want the display lit before the busiest shopping weeks, which means planning in late summer or early fall. If that window has passed, call anyway and we will tell you what is still possible.
Can you install without disrupting tenants?
We plan installation around store hours, deliveries and parking, and confirm the schedule with property management before the crew arrives.
Can you light more than one property?
Yes. Property managers can bundle several centers or buildings into one plan with one point of contact for the season.
verticals.summary: Building outlines, parking lot trees and pole decor that help a shopping center stand out from the road.
verticals.cta_line: Book a walkthrough for your center.

needs: A welcoming entrance

Minimal disruption
Installs are scheduled around business hours and parking, with lift work planned to stay clear of the main entry.
Easy for facilities teams
One estimate, one schedule and one contact for installation, in-season service and removal.
scope: Bistro lighting for courtyards and patios
faqs: Can installation happen around our business hours?
Yes. We plan installation around your hours and parking, and confirm the schedule with your facilities contact before the crew arrives.
Do you work with property managers?
Yes. We work with owners, facilities teams and property managers, and we can plan several buildings together.
Can we start with the entrance and add more later?
Yes. Many businesses start with the entrance and main sign, then add trees or rooflines in later seasons. We plan it so each addition fits the whole.

about.title: About Holiday Light Service | Lighting Since 2003
about.meta_description: Holiday Light Service has lit Southeast Michigan since 2003. See how we plan, install, service and take down displays for homes, businesses and downtowns.
about.intro: For more than twenty years, Holiday Light Service has put up lights that make people slow down and look, on homes, storefronts, neighborhood entrances and downtown streets.
story: Holiday Light Service has been lighting Southeast Michigan since 2003, and the idea behind it is simple. People love a lit house in December. Very few of them love climbing a ladder in the cold to make it happen. So we do it for them.

Over two decades, that work has covered rooflines and front-yard trees, HOA entrances and downtown streets wrapped block by block, and shopping centers, offices and other businesses get the same careful planning. Bucket trucks handle the high work. The approach is straightforward: plan it carefully, install it cleanly, service it through the season and take it down when the season is over.
We also install permanent roofline lighting and landscape lighting, for homeowners and businesses who want their property to look good well past the holidays.
Holiday Light Service is now part of the Ace Outdoor Services family.
values: Straight rooflines, even spacing and tidy wraps. The details are what people see from the street.
We treat your roof, gutters, trees and landscaping with care, and clean up before we leave.
Your estimate spells out what is included, so you know what you are getting before the crew shows up.
Bucket trucks handle the tall and steep work wherever the property allows. When ice or high wind moves in, high work waits for a better day.
about.services_intro: Rooflines and trees at home, full-season displays for businesses and downtowns, and permanent and landscape lighting that keeps working after the holidays end.

faq.title: Holiday Lighting FAQ | Holiday Light Service
faq.meta_description: Answers about Christmas light installation timing, estimates, HOA approvals, power, weather, takedown and permanent lighting in Southeast Michigan.
faq.intro: The questions people usually ask before they book. If yours is not here, call us and ask.
items: How far ahead should I book Christmas light installation?

The earlier the better. Installs commonly run from October into early December, and booking in September or October gives you the most choice of dates. Later requests are still worth a call, but options narrow as Thanksgiving gets close.
When do the lights go up and come down?
Most installs happen between October and early December, so the display is ready for the season. Takedown happens after the holidays, commonly in January.
What is included in your service?
Design, installation, in-season service and takedown after the season. Your estimate spells out exactly what is included for your property.
How do estimates work?
Estimates are free. Call us or use the request form, and we will look at the property, plan the layout and send a written estimate.
Do I need HOA approval?

It depends on your association. Some have rules about exterior lighting, especially permanent fixtures, so check your guidelines. Our estimate describes the layout, which gives your board something clear to consider.
Do commercial projects start with a walkthrough?
Yes. Commercial, HOA and municipal projects start with a site walkthrough to look at the buildings, trees, power and lift access. The concept design and estimate come from that visit.
What is the difference between permanent and seasonal lighting?

Seasonal lights go up in the fall and come down after the holidays. Permanent lighting mounts in a discreet track under the eaves and stays up all year, controlled from an app. Seasonal suits a classic December display. Permanent suits people who want lights for more occasions.
Do you offer landscape lighting?
Yes. We design and install landscape lighting that highlights architecture, trees and walkways after dark, all year. It can be planned alongside your holiday lighting.
What areas do you serve?
Southeast Michigan, centered on Oakland, Genesee and Livingston counties, plus nearby communities in Wayne and Macomb counties. If you are not sure, send your address and we will confirm.
What happens if the weather is bad on install day?
Michigan fall weather is part of the job, and crews work in the cold. When ice, heavy rain or high wind make roof or lift work unsafe, we reschedule and let you know the new plan.
Can you reach tall trees and two-story rooflines?
Yes. Bucket-truck crews handle tall trees, steep peaks and two-story rooflines wherever the property allows. During the estimate we check access, ground conditions and anything overhead.
Do I need extra outlets or power?

Often not. During the estimate we look at where your exterior outlets are and how circuits are shared, then plan the layout around them. If a design needs more power than you have, we will tell you before installation.
How should I prepare for installation?

Make sure the crew can reach exterior outlets, gates and the areas being lit. Keep the driveway clear if the bucket truck needs it, and tell us about pets, locked gates or anything fragile near the house.
What if some lights stop working during the season?
Call us. In-season service is part of what we do, and we will set up a service visit for the section that went out.

guides.title: When to Book Christmas Light Installation in Michigan
guides.meta_description: A practical timeline for booking Christmas light installation in Michigan: when to call, when installs happen and what to decide before the rush.
guides.h1: When to book Christmas light installation in Michigan
guides.dek: A simple season timeline, from the first call in early fall to takedown in January, and what to decide at each step.

sections.heading: A short season with a fixed finish line
paragraphs: Professional Christmas light installation runs on a short calendar. Many homeowners want their lights up by Thanksgiving or the first weekend of December, and installers across Michigan are working toward the same handful of weeks. A crew can only be in so many driveways at once, and the weather decides some of the days for you.

That is why the day you call matters so much. Call early and you choose your install date. Call late and you choose from what is left. The display itself can be exactly the same either way. The difference is how much choice you have, and how relaxed the process feels.

sections.heading: September: start the conversation
paragraphs: Early fall is the easiest time to plan. The weather is mild, the calendar is open and there is time to think about the design instead of rushing it. It is also a good moment to step outside at dusk and look at your house the way the street sees it. Which rooflines stand out? Which trees are worth lighting? Where are your outdoor outlets?

If you had lights last year, think about what you liked and what you would change. If this is your first professional install, jot down the look you want: warm white or multicolor, just the roofline or the trees too. You do not need a finished plan. A rough idea is plenty to start an estimate.

sections.heading: October: design, estimate and scheduling
paragraphs: October is when most planning turns into a schedule. Your installer looks at the property, maps out the rooflines, trees and power, and sends an estimate that spells out what is included. Once you approve it, you get an install date.

Installs commonly start in October. That can feel early, but lights installed in late October or early November can simply stay off until you want them on. Nobody has to see your display before Thanksgiving unless you want them to. Booking in this window makes it far more likely that everything is ready for the first holiday gathering at your house.

Before you approve an estimate, confirm three things: what gets lit, how in-season service works if a section goes dark, and when takedown happens after the holidays. A clear answer to each now saves a phone call in December.

sections.heading: November: the busiest stretch
paragraphs: November is when the calendar fills. The days are shorter, the weather is less predictable and a lot of people decide at the same moment that this is the year they stop climbing the ladder. Requests made in November can still work out, but the choice of dates is narrower.

If you are booking in November, be flexible. Have a couple of possible dates in mind, make sure outlets and gates are easy to reach, and mention anything that could slow the crew down, such as a locked side yard or a car that lives in the driveway.

It also helps to decide quickly. When dates are filling, the gap between getting an estimate and approving it is often what separates the date you wanted from the one you get. Have your questions ready, and loop in anyone else who needs to weigh in before the estimate arrives.

sections.heading: Early December and late requests
paragraphs: It is still worth calling in early December. Installs commonly run into early December, and a focused display on the front roofline and the trees facing the street can still make the season feel complete.

Late requests are about priorities. Light what people see from the street first, keep the design simple and save the bigger ideas for next year. A clean, well-installed roofline looks better than a rushed display that tries to cover everything.

sections.heading: January: takedown and a head start on next year
paragraphs: After the holidays, the lights come down. Takedown commonly happens in January, once the season is over, so the house can go back to normal for the rest of winter.

January is also the easiest time to remember what worked. Maybe the trees stole the show, or the side of the house felt dark. Make a note while it is fresh. When fall comes around again, you will call earlier with a clearer idea, and that is how you end up with the dates you want.

guides.title: Permanent vs Seasonal Holiday Lights: How to Choose
guides.meta_description: Permanent or seasonal holiday lights? Compare how each works, how each looks and how you will use them, and find the right fit for your home and HOA.
guides.h1: Permanent vs seasonal holiday lights: how to choose
guides.dek: Both can make a house look sharp in December. The real difference is how you want to use your lights the other eleven months of the year.

sections.heading: How seasonal holiday lighting works
paragraphs: Seasonal lighting is the classic approach. Strands go up along the roofline, around tree trunks and across shrubs in the fall, stay lit through the holidays and come down after the season. With professional installation, the crew designs the display, installs it, services it during the season and takes it down in January.

Seasonal lighting is flexible. You can light the roofline one year and add the trees the next, switch from multicolor to warm white, or go bigger for a year when family is coming to town. Because nothing stays attached all year, the house looks exactly as it always does from January to fall.

The trade-off is the calendar. Seasonal lighting means an install date every fall and a takedown date every winter, which works well for people who like the ritual of the season and do not mind planning around it.

sections.heading: How permanent lighting works
paragraphs: Permanent lighting mounts in a discreet track under the eaves and stays up all year. The lights are controlled from a smartphone app, where you choose colors, set scenes and schedule when the lights turn on and off.

Because it is always there, permanent lighting is less about one season and more about having light whenever you want it. Warm white for Christmas, orange for Halloween, team colors for a big game, soft accent light on an ordinary weeknight. There is no install date to book each fall and nothing to take down in January.

sections.heading: How they look, day and night
paragraphs: At night, both can look sharp. Seasonal lighting has a traditional look that many people love, and it works on trees and shrubs as well as the house. Permanent lighting gives the roofline a clean, even outline in whatever color you choose that evening.

During the day, the difference is what you see. Seasonal lights are on the roofline during the season and gone the rest of the year. Permanent track sits under the eaves in a low profile, so it is discreet, but it is there year round. Look at your trim, your roofline and your street, and think about which trade-off suits you.

sections.heading: How often you will actually use them
paragraphs: This is the question that usually decides it. If you only want lights in December and you love the classic look, seasonal lighting fits. If you can picture using lights for birthdays, other holidays, game days or everyday accent lighting, permanent lighting deserves a close look.

Think about convenience too. Some homeowners like having the roofline softly lit every night on a schedule, without thinking about it. Permanent lighting can do that all year. Seasonal lighting is built for one season.

sections.heading: Questions to ask before you decide
paragraphs: Does your HOA have rules about exterior lighting or permanent fixtures? Check your guidelines before you commit. An estimate that describes the layout and hardware gives your board something clear to consider.

What do you want lit besides the roofline? Permanent lighting is designed for the roofline. Trees, shrubs and entrances are usually lit seasonally. If your favorite part of the display is a wrapped maple or a row of evergreens, you may want both.
How do you feel about planning each fall? Seasonal lighting means booking an install date every year. Permanent lighting means one installation and an app on your phone.

How long do you plan to stay in the house? Permanent lighting is a longer-term choice for the house, while seasonal lighting is a decision you make one year at a time. Both are reasonable. They simply fit different plans.

sections.heading: You do not have to choose only one
paragraphs: Plenty of homes work well with a mix: permanent lighting on the roofline for year-round use, with seasonal wraps on the trees and shrubs each December. The roofline is always ready, and the yard still gets the full holiday treatment.

If you are still undecided, start with an estimate. We will look at your home, talk through how you plan to use the lights and spell out what each option includes, so you can compare them side by side. Bring your questions about the look, the app and your HOA, and we will answer them plainly.

guides.title: Planning Commercial Holiday Lighting: A Practical Guide
guides.meta_description: How property managers, HOA boards and downtowns plan commercial holiday lighting: goals, walkthroughs, power, approvals, scheduling and season service.
guides.h1: Planning commercial holiday lighting: a practical guide
guides.dek: For property managers, HOA boards and downtown teams: how to plan a display that looks deliberate, stays lit and runs on schedule.

sections.heading: Start with what the lighting has to do
paragraphs: Commercial holiday lighting always has a job. A shopping center wants drivers to notice it from the road. A downtown wants people to stay for dinner after the tree lighting. An HOA wants residents to feel good pulling into the neighborhood. An office wants clients and employees to see a property that looks cared for.

Write down the job before anything else. It decides where the lighting goes, how much of the property needs it and what can wait for a future season. It also gives everyone involved, from the board to the installer, the same goal to measure the design against.

sections.heading: Look at the property at night
paragraphs: A property looks different after dark. Drive the main approach at night. Walk from the parking lot to the entrance. Notice what is already lit, what disappears and what catches your eye first. The buildings, trees and poles you notice at night are usually the ones worth lighting.

Take a few photos from the spots that matter most: the main road, the parking lot, the front door and any gathering space. Those photos make the walkthrough faster and help everyone agree on what the display needs to accomplish.

Then schedule a walkthrough with your installer. A good walkthrough covers the buildings, trees, poles and entrances, and turns them into a concept design and an estimate you can take to a board or an owner.

sections.heading: Power, access and safety
paragraphs: Commercial displays involve longer runs and more power sources than a home. Know where the exterior outlets are, which circuits they share and whether some areas have no power at all. Your installer should map this during the walkthrough and plan the design around it.

Access matters just as much. Bucket trucks need somewhere to park, and lift work near entrances, sidewalks and traffic has to be planned. Point out loading zones, fire lanes, soft ground, irrigation and anything overhead, so installation day does not turn into problem solving.

Name one person on your side as the contact for the season. Installers need someone who can answer questions about access, approve small changes on site and report a section that goes dark. When that role is clear, everything else moves faster.

sections.heading: Approvals, budgets and timing
paragraphs: Boards, downtown development authorities and ownership groups meet on their own calendars. Build approval time into your plan. Starting the conversation in late summer or early fall leaves time to share a concept, adjust it and still land a good install date.

Budgets go further when you prioritize. Light what people see first, then add depth over time. A plan that grows over a few seasons often looks more deliberate than one that tries to do everything in year one.
Give decision makers something concrete. A concept design, a clear list of what gets lit and a written estimate make approval far easier than a general description and a total.

sections.heading: Schedule around the business
paragraphs: Installation and removal should work around store hours, deliveries, events and parking. Share those details early. Your installer can then plan crew days and lift work around your busiest times and confirm the schedule before anyone arrives.

If the property hosts a tree lighting, a holiday market or a grand opening, put the date in writing at the start. Working backward from a fixed event is the simplest way to keep a commercial install on track.

sections.heading: Plan the whole season, not just install day
paragraphs: A display is only as good as it looks in the middle of December. Ask how in-season service works, who to call when a section goes dark and when removal happens after the holidays. Your estimate should spell out what is included, from design to takedown.
Finally, keep a record of what worked. Photos from this season make next year's planning faster, and a design that works can be repeated with small changes.

If you manage several buildings or blocks, keep the look consistent. Mixing warm and cool whites, or lighting one building fully and the next one halfway, reads as unplanned from the street. One design language across the property makes the whole place feel intentional.

guides.title: Holiday Lights Without the Ladder | Holiday Light Service
guides.meta_description: What a DIY holiday light display really takes, what full-service Christmas light installation covers and how to hand off the ladder this year.
guides.dek: What a do-it-yourself display really takes, what full-service installation covers, and how to hand off the ladder this year.

sections.heading: What a DIY display really takes
paragraphs: On paper, putting up Christmas lights is a Saturday project. In practice, it starts with finding last year's strands in the garage, testing them, making another run to the store and working out how to reach the peak over the garage. Then comes the ladder, the clips and the cold.

The second half of the job is easy to forget. The lights have to stay up through snow and wind, and sometimes a strand goes dark in the middle of December. After the holidays, everything has to come down again, usually on a day nobody wants to be outside.

Add it up and a modest display can eat into more than one weekend across the season, plus the evenings spent troubleshooting a strand that will not light. For a lot of homeowners, that time is the real cost.

sections.heading: Where DIY goes wrong
paragraphs: Ladders on frozen ground, wet shingles and second-story peaks are where the real risk is. Holiday lights are not worth a fall. Rooflines also tend to look homemade when the spacing drifts, the strands sag between clips and the whites do not match from one box to the next.

Then there is power. Too many strands on one outlet trips breakers, extension cords end up across walkways and timers get forgotten. None of it is hard to fix, but it takes time most people do not have in December.

Finally, there is the house itself. Leaning a ladder against gutters can bend them, and fasteners that go into shingles or trim can leave marks long after the lights are gone. A careful installer plans how lights attach to each surface before anything goes up.

sections.heading: What full-service installation covers
paragraphs: With professional Christmas light installation, you describe the look and the crew handles the rest. That means designing a layout around your roofline, trees and entry, installing it with even spacing and clean lines, and testing it before leaving.

It also covers the season. If a section goes dark, you make a call instead of climbing. After the holidays, the crew comes back for takedown. Your estimate spells out what is included, so you know what to expect from the first visit to the last.
Crews with bucket trucks can reach tall trees and steep peaks that are unsafe from a ladder. That high work is often where a display gets its biggest impact.

sections.heading: What you still get to decide
paragraphs: Hiring out the work does not mean giving up the look. You decide warm white or multicolor, just the roofline or the trees too, and how the display should feel from the street. Some homeowners want a quiet, classic outline. Others want every tree wrapped to the top.

If you have ideas from photos or from a house you admire on your street, share them. A good installer will tell you what will work on your home, what to leave out and where a little restraint looks better than more lights.

You also decide the scale. A sensible first year is the front roofline and the trees closest to the street. If you love the result, add the side of the house, the backyard or the bistro lights over the patio next season. The design can grow with you, one year at a time.

sections.heading: How to get started
paragraphs: Start early. Installs commonly run from October into early December, and earlier requests get more choice of dates.

Before you hire anyone, ask a few simple questions. What exactly is included? How does in-season service work if something goes dark? When does takedown happen? How will the lights attach to your roof and gutters? How will the crew reach the high sections? Clear answers tell you a lot about how the season will go.

Walk around your house at dusk and note what you want lit and where your outdoor outlets are. Then call or send a request with your address. Estimates are free. The only ladder you will need this year is the step stool for the star on the tree.
